author: potuz
content: Hey <@592004585506340885> there's an issue raised by <@884836500037066862> in Prysm that kinda worried me. We record equivocations for forkchoice regardless if the blocks are valid or not. I think this is correct and the intended behavior. But it is true that it may trigger a split if other clients treat this differently, so asking here if we have a test for this case or not. cc <@520034910149410861> in case this is **not** the intended behavior.

author: potuz
content: <@520034910149410861> the attack case here is kinda interesting cause you can broadcast early an invalid block, and then later the valid equivocating block. In this case you may cause an ex-ante reorg if the invalid block is counting as an equivocation cause then the incoming block, which can only be based on the valid equivocating block, may lose proposer boost.
